Title: Tool Verification for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
Summary: This visual presents a flow diagram illustrating the concept of Tool Verification for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning (T²RL). It highlights the process of verifying pseudo-labels generated through majority voting, emphasizing the importance of accurate sampled predictions and estimated rewards. The diagram includes key components such as the verifier, which utilizes external tools to enhance the reliability of predictions. Additionally, it showcases comparative results across various benchmarks, indicating significant improvements in accuracy when employing T²RL. The visual effectively communicates the methodology and benefits of integrating verification in reinforcement learning to mitigate issues related to spurious pseudo-labels.

Title: Tool Verification for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
Summary: This visual is a flow diagram illustrating the process of tool verification for test-time reinforcement learning (TRL). It depicts how an LLM verifier parses sampled outputs from a model, yielding validity flags for each output. The diagram shows the integration of a code interpreter that executes the sampled outputs to validate them. Key components include the sampling of predictions, the generation of estimated rewards, and the use of majority voting to derive consensus outputs. The process highlights the challenges of spurious reward estimation in self-evolving AI systems, emphasizing the importance of reliable reward signals for stable online learning.

Title: Comparison of Improvement Metrics for Math Levels
Summary: This bar chart compares the improvement percentages across different math levels (MATH-L1 to MATH-L5) for two methods: TTRL and T³RL. The y-axis represents the percentage of improvement, while the x-axis lists the math levels. MATH-L1 shows the highest improvement at over 250%, followed by MATH-L2 with a modest increase of 0.5%. The T³RL method demonstrates a consistent upward trend in additional gain, peaking at 8.9% for MATH-L5. Overall, the chart highlights the effectiveness of the T³RL method in achieving higher improvements across the math levels compared to TTRL.

Title: Comparison of Scores in AIME and MATH
Summary: This bar chart compares scores in two assessments, AIME and MATH, across different categories. The left section displays scores for TTRL and various 'No Code' categories, with TTRL achieving a score of 20.0 in AIME and 73.6 in MATH. The middle section shows the same 'No Code' categories, with scores of 18.3 for AIME and 73.1 for MATH. The right section introduces a new category, 'With Code', showing a score of 21.7 in AIME and 74.9 in MATH. The data indicates a trend where the 'With Code' category outperforms the 'No Code' categories in both assessments, highlighting the impact of coding on performance.

Summary: This visual consists of two charts illustrating the accuracy gains associated with different methodologies in a machine learning context. Title: Math Computation Verification Process
Summary: This flow diagram illustrates the process of verifying a mathematical computation involving the expression 992 + 99 + 1. It begins with a query to compute the expression, followed by two approaches: one using a language model (LLM) and the other a verifier. The LLM incorrectly rewrites the expression and arrives at an erroneous result of 10000, while the verifier correctly breaks down the computation into steps, ultimately arriving at the accurate result of 9901. The diagram highlights the importance of step-by-step verification to ensure accuracy in mathematical calculations.
